pull.title: cmpctblock: Cache serialized cmpctblock msg for relay [part of prefill series]
pull.body:
This PR extends the optimization added in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/23880 which applies to peers that have requested HB blocks from us to also cache the serialized blocks for low-bandwidth peers. The core change here comes from the closed #26755 made by andrewtoth, but also includes other refactors and type safety improvements.

Performance is less critical for low-bandwidth peers, so this change on its own should have little impact on block propagation, but these refactors are useful as part of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35558 which adds prefilling of compact blocks, and where we run the risk of potentially having to serialize more than one cmpctblock_msg (one prefilled and one not-prefilled).

events.message:
p2p: Cache serialized `cmpct_block_msg` for relay.

This commit is drawn from the closed #26755.
(https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/26755)

This also changes `std::launch::deferred` to `std::launch::async` since
we are likely going to use this result very soon if someone has
requested HB blocks from us, and if no one has, then performance here is
not that critical.

Co-authored-by: Andrew Toth <andrewstoth@gmail.com>

net: refactor: Move common logic into SendCompactBlock

Also one non-refactor change which is setting the `pIndexBestHeaderSent`
on the `SendMessages` CMPCTBLOCK announcement fallback.

qa: Make PeerHasHeader more robust against nullptr

Noticed while making changes to compact blocks code, right now
`PeerHasHeader` relies on callers to never make the mistake of calling
it with a nullptr, `state` can be trivially made into a reference, and
we can add an Assume for pindex being nullptr, and fall back to returning
false.

comments.body:
for reference, the reason I didn't pick async was that this would create an unnamed/global/unscoped/hidden thread pool. I guess this should be fine, but the commit msg could say that this will introduce a new thread(pool) beside the named threads:

```
  myprogram    # main
  myprogram    # std::async worker, usually unnamed
  initload ,...    # named TraceThreads/ named Pools
```

<details><summary>edit: Also ralph says this, while it is likely ai slop, it highlights that this is not a trivial change and reviewers would have to look at the error handling path in this line</summary>

```
🟠 Minor · Thread-launch failure interrupts block acceptance before storage

Under local thread-resource exhaustion, the forced async launch can interrupt acceptance of a new tip-extending block before storage, although a retry can recover.
```

</details>
nit: While changing the log output, could remove all the fluent/redundant `__func__` or reword them to something hard-coded and unique. (Also, drop the trailing newlines, while touching.
